concerns.text: SC-001 (and US-1-AS-1) sets a time bound of '≤ 60 seconds' but does not define the hardware baseline (e.g., specific CPU model, clock speed, or cloud instance type) against which this is measured. 'Standard CPU instance' is not a reproducible test condition.

US-1-AS-2 requires the sequence to 'consist of valid PDDL-like predicates' but does not define the schema, grammar, or validator used to determine 'validity'. Without a formal grammar or reference validator, this cannot be deterministically verified.

US-2-AS-1 relies on 'task completion criteria defined in the RoboDojo benchmark' but does not specify which of the 18 tasks or how the binary pass/fail is programmatically determined (e.g., specific sensor thresholds, object pose tolerances). This is not independently verifiable without external documentation.

US-2-AS-2 sets a wall-clock limit of '≤ 4 hours' for 18 tasks but does not account for variable execution times or define the concurrency model (sequential vs. parallel). The test is ambiguous regarding whether this is total elapsed time or cumulative CPU time.

US-3-AS-1 requires a 'Wilcoxon signed-rank test' but does not specify the null hypothesis formulation (e.g., median difference = 0) or the handling of ties/zero differences, which affects the p-value calculation and reproducibility.

SC-005 measures 'rate of catastrophic failures' against a 'null hypothesis expectation of catastrophic failure'. This is circular; the null hypothesis is a statistical construct, not a measurable rate. The criterion needs a specific threshold (e.g., 'failure rate < 5%') to be measurable.
